presentingComplaint: Known cirrhotic with 3 days of low-grade fever, worsening abdominal distension and diffuse abdominal discomfort.
history: Alcohol-related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B) with recurrent ascites managed on diuretics; two prior large-volume paracenteses. Over 3 days he has developed low-grade fever, increasing abdominal girth, mild diffuse abdominal pain and reduced appetite. Family note he has become slightly drowsy and muddled today. No haematemesis or melena. No recent antibiotics or hospitalisation. No prior SBP episode.
examination: Ill-appearing, mildly icteric. Tense ascites with diffuse mild tenderness and reduced bowel sounds; no localised guarding or rigidity. Grade 1-2 asterixis and inattention. Spider naevi, palmar erythema. No cellulitis or focal source. Chest clear; no CVA tenderness or dysuria.
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound: coarse cirrhotic liver, splenomegaly, moderate-to-large ascites, patent portal vein; no bowel perforation, abscess or biliary obstruction (helps exclude secondary peritonitis).
microbiology: Ascitic fluid inoculated into blood-culture bottles at bedside; Gram-negative bacilli / E. coli commonly isolated. Blood cultures x2 sent.
citations: Harrison 22e — Cirrhosis and Its Complications (Ascites and SBP)
AASLD Management of Ascites and SBP in Cirrhosis 2021
stewardship: Empiric third-generation cephalosporin (IV cefotaxime 2 g q8h, or ceftriaxone 2 g daily) started immediately on ascitic PMN >=250/mm3, before culture results. Add IV albumin 1.5 g/kg day 1 and 1 g/kg day 3 to reduce hepatorenal syndrome and mortality. Escalate to piperacillin-tazobactam or a carbapenem if nosocomial/recent beta-lactam exposure or local ESBL prevalence.
contraindications: Nephrotoxins/aminoglycosides best avoided given renal impairment and HRS risk
Dose-adjust for renal function; monitor creatinine
Avoid NSAIDs and non-selective beta-blocker uptitration during acute SBP/hypotension
edgeCases: Culture-negative neutrocytic ascites (PMN >=250 but sterile culture) — treat as SBP
Bacterascites (positive culture, PMN <250) — treat if symptomatic
Polymicrobial growth, PMN very high, or failure to respond should trigger search for SECONDARY peritonitis (perforation) with CT and surgical review
expectedMaiK: In a cirrhotic with ascites, fever/abdominal pain/encephalopathy mandates diagnostic paracentesis; an ascitic PMN >=250 cells/mm3 establishes SBP and warrants immediate empiric cefotaxime plus IV albumin. A single organism and high SAAG support primary SBP, while polymicrobial or very high-PMN fluid should prompt exclusion of secondary peritonitis.
expectedNextQuestions: Any recent GI bleed, prior SBP episodes, or antibiotic prophylaxis (norfloxacin/ciprofloxacin)?
Any localised peritonism or recent instrumentation suggesting a surgical/secondary cause?
expectedInvestigations: Diagnostic paracentesis with ascitic fluid cell count/differential, culture in blood-culture bottles, total protein and SAAG
Blood cultures, renal function and lactate before antibiotics

investigations: Diagnostic paracentesis with ascitic PMN count and culture

regressionAssertions: ascitic PMN >=250 with high SAAG should not rank secondary peritonitis above SBP without polymicrobial/localising features
